A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same M-ABSA study. All 28 pages of each version, including Appendices A-I, tables, figures, and mathematical expressions, support reliable comparison without material reading gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original automatic and human translation-quality evaluations, mT5 transfer experiments, and LLM evaluations in Sections 5-6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including human ratings in Table 4, mT5 results in Table 5, and detailed appendix evaluations.

M1.justification: The dataset construction, numbered-marker translation and annotation projection, manual correction, mT5 modeling, and LLM prompts are unchanged. Knowledge- and retrieval-augmented approaches are mentioned only as future directions.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same seven domains and 21 languages, TASD and UABSA tasks, and cross-lingual, cross-domain, and translation-quality scenarios. Section 5.1 alphabetizes the existing target-language list without changing membership.

E2.justification: The evaluated models remain mT5-base, Llama-3.1 8B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B, and Qwen-2.5 7B. The random-pair translation baseline is also retained. Newly cited methods are not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Data splits, model sizes, training settings, micro-F1 evaluation, and translation-quality protocols are unchanged. Both retain 1,050 sampled items per language for automatic evaluation and 70 sentences per language across eight languages for human evaluation.

E4.justification: The source-language analyses, t-SNE visualizations, cross-domain analyses, and translation-error examples are retained with the same evidence. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Section 6.1 retains reporting averages over five random seeds. Neither version adds confidence intervals, significance tests, or a different uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Numerical results and reported findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 5 retains English average F1 scores of 47.68 for TASD and 66.68 for UABSA; Tables 7-31 and the result plots are unchanged.

T1.justification: Task formulations, metric descriptions, and annotation definitions are unchanged. Neither version contains a theoretical contribution that is added, removed, or revised; spacing changes in Appendix B's equation example are typographical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same dataset, construction-method, and evaluation contributions. Replacing 'multiple domains' with '7 domains' in a contribution bullet restates coverage already explicit in v2.

C2.justification: Section 8 adds knowledge- and retrieval-augmented approaches as possible responses to the existing specialized-model limitation. Section 9 removes the stated aim of promoting social-media and public-opinion analysis across countries. Other limitations and result interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The appendices retain the same annotation instructions, proofreading procedures, mT5 hyperparameters, evaluation packages and models, and prompts. Code and dataset access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Mai et al. (2024) on GEDA in Section 2.3 and Zhang et al. (2022, 2024) on knowledge-enhanced ABSA and MAR in Section 8. Wu et al. is updated from its 2024 preprint to its 2025 journal reference, representing the same work.

P1.justification: Local edits specify seven domains in the contribution list, alphabetize languages, correct 'Gemme-2' to 'Gemma-2', and revise short related-work, future-work, and ethics passages. The overall narrative and section order remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds bold emphasis to contribution bullets and makes small layout adjustments, including moving Table 6 from the left to the right column on page 15. Appendix text and Figure 7 shift locally; no figure or table is added, removed, or substantively redesigned.

improvement.justification: v3 supplies limited bibliographic context and editorial polish while preserving the dataset documentation, empirical evidence, and reproducibility information. The expanded future-work suggestion does not materially develop the existing limitations. These local changes leave the paper's overall quality essentially unchanged.
